draft.subject_line: Reconciliation between IaC and cluster state
draft.body:
The FunnelFox launch absorbed six PSP integrations into a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster in twelve days — every PSP added new IAM roles, new secret stores, new network policies, all declared in IaC and all subject to drift the moment the next iteration ships.

The reconciliation question — where IaC says X but the cluster and cloud actually do Y — doesn't usually surface until something breaks at the worst possible time, since static IaC checks run on a different cadence than the cluster's actual change rate.

Transilience reconciles IaC-declared state against effective cluster state continuously — IAM, secrets, and network policy together — surfacing drift before it accumulates into incidents.

Has declared-vs-effective checking been pulled into the deploy pipeline, or is it still incident-driven?
draft.architecture: signal-to-question — operational triangulation in opener (FunnelFox + 6 PSPs + self-hosted k8s + IaC), names the reconciliation gap (declared X vs actual Y), product sentence anchored in IAM/secrets/network policy specificity, binary technical CTA

verdict_history.reason: Strongest CTA of the four Adapty drafts. Correctly assumes security-vocabulary fluency throughout. Binary CTA ('pipeline or incident-driven?') is a real engineering question that invites a substantive answer.

witness.what_works: Operational triangulation in opener uses concrete public artifacts (FunnelFox + 6 PSPs + self-hosted k8s). Names the reconciliation problem in his exact intellectual frame (declared X vs actual Y — same gap his DDD library exists to prevent in code). 'Reconciles' verb is distinct from extends/does/handling. CTA is a real engineering binary that invites a one-line answer.
witness.what_fails: 'Twelve days' anchor still appears here (and in Kirill) — 2/4 Adapty drafts. Acceptable given it's a factual anchor for the operational pace question, not a stylistic tic.
